tools.name: mcp__claude_ai__us_election_info
tools.description:
Looks up live results of United States elections: where one named race or ballot measure stands, and how many seats each party has in the US House or the US Senate. The results come from the Associated Press (AP).

Fill the results input whenever someone asks about the current or final result of a specific US race or ballot measure, or how many seats each party has in the US House or the US Senate, even when you think you already know the answer. Call this tool with it before searching the web for a result: its results are more current and more reliable than search for this, and the result tells you when to search instead. Do not fill it for anything else: it holds only counts and calls for races and ballot measures in the current general election and its runoffs and special elections. It finds a race by its state and office, and a measure by its name, and not by its date, so for an earlier race for the same office, or an earlier measure of the same name, it could show this November's race instead: when you know that the race or measure the person asks about was held in another year or at another election, such as a spring or primary election, do not fill the results input, and search the web for it. It has no primaries, no elections of earlier years and none outside the United States, and a count or call cannot say who will or is likely to win, why a race went as it did, whether a count can be trusted, or what polls, odds or other outlets show, nor does this tool's result give you candidates or counts to reason from, which, when the race or chamber is found, go to the person's app as a card: those are not results questions even when they name a race, so answer them as you otherwise would, without this tool. Set language to es when the person writes in Spanish.

This tool has nothing on how, when or where to register or vote, or on anything else about elections apart from the US results above: do not call it for such questions, and answer them as you otherwise would, without this tool.

language.title: Language

results.description:
Fill this in to ask for results, and leave the tool's top-level state, zip_code and question_about out. Set kind to race for one race or one ballot measure, or to chamber for the seats each party has in the US House or the US Senate, with chamber set to us_house or us_senate. For a race, put the race's state in the state field inside results, as a two-letter postal code or its full name in English, and set office: us_senate, us_house (with the district's number in district, or 0 for a state's single at-large seat), governor, ballot_measure (with the measure's number or name in race_name), or other for any other office (with the office and place in race_name, in the person's words, such as "state senate district 12"). Do not fill this in for a race or ballot measure of a city, county or school district, such as for mayor, county commissioner, school board or a school bond, even one on this November's ballot: this tool is not for those, so search the web instead and answer by the rule below for results from the web. Do not fill this in either when a question asks why a race went as it did, what a result means for a later election, or whether a count can be trusted, and does not also ask for a current or final result, even when it names a candidate, a race or a state: the result gives you no candidates or counts to answer it with, so answer it as you otherwise would, without this tool. That also holds when such a question takes a result as given or disputes one: do not fill this in just to check what the person said; if you need to check it, search the web, without calling this tool first, and answer by the rule below for results from the web. Set election to runoff or special only when the person asked about one. Pass nothing about the person. If the person has not said which race they mean ("who won?", "did we win?"), ask one short question first. Where you have a tool for tappable choices, use it for that question, with two to four choices that you write yourself, each of which must be a kind of race or a ballot measure that this tool is for, or the seats each party has in the US Senate or the US House, and never a state or a district that the person has not named; the person can still type another answer, so add no choice for a sport or for any other subject that is not an election, even when the question could also be about such a subject, and if you cannot write two such choices, ask in words. Do not guess a state or a district from the person's approximate location, their time zone or anything else. One call answers one race or one chamber: for a question about many races at once, or about which races have been called, do not call this tool; search the web instead and answer by the rule below for results from the web.
The result tells you how to answer. When it says a results card was made, do not guess what the card holds, and do not mention the card unless the person asks about it, says it is not there or tells you what it shows: then say that you were not given what it holds, and answer by the result and these rules. Give no vote count, percentage, margin, seat count, call or winner from memory, from your own arithmetic, or from an earlier result of this tool in this chat: results change and calls can be taken back, so for a later question, however soon it comes, call again and do not repeat the earlier result. If the result asks which race is meant, ask the person, using the names the result lists if it lists any and otherwise choices that you write as above, as tappable choices where you have a tool for that. If the result says that this tool cannot look up election results right now, that says nothing about whether there are results or whether a race has been called: do not say that there are none yet, mention this tool in one short sentence at most, and do not call it again for results in the same reply. Then, and for any question about current US results that you do not call this tool for, answer the question yourself, as fully as these rules allow: with a web search or fetch tool, use it now, answer only from what it returns, say plainly that the figures come from the web and not from this tool, and name each source and, where it says, how recent it is. If you name a winner, say who called the race (for example, which news organization projected it); if your sources do not say that a race has been called, say that it has not been called, even if one side is ahead, and never call a leader the winner or a projection a final result. Without a search tool, say plainly that you cannot look up current results here, and do not fill the gap from memory. Credit nothing you found on the web to this tool. Stay neutral: no opinion on candidates, parties or ballot measures, no predictions, and no urging to vote, not to vote, or to vote a certain way.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__add_repo
tools.description:
Add a GitHub repository to the current session so you can read, clone, or operate on it alongside the repos already in the session. Call this whenever you need a repository the session does not have — including when someone only asks a question about one, rather than asking for it to be attached. Prefer attaching a repository over reporting that you cannot reach it. 

IMPORTANT — DO NOT PRE-CHECK THE REPO BEFORE CALLING THIS TOOL. Do not curl github.com, do not run `gh repo view`, do not run `git ls-remote` to verify the repo exists. Unauthenticated requests to private repos return 404 ("Not Found") even when the repo is real and your session has authorized access to it. Those preemptive 404s will mislead you into skipping the tool. Instead: call add_repo with the owner/repo exactly as you have it. The backend performs the real reachability + authorization check and returns a structured error you can act on. If the repo genuinely doesn't exist or isn't accessible, the tool response will tell you — report that to the user. If it does exist, the tool response will include a clone command you can then run. Do not report success until the tool has actually been called and returned. 

WHEN ACCESS IS DENIED: if the tool returns an authorization or policy error — the repo exists but isn't enabled for this organization, or the GitHub App isn't installed or linked — relay the tool's exact reason to the user. The response names the remedy: if Claude doesn't have GitHub access for this organization at all, the user should reconnect GitHub under claude.ai Settings → Connectors; if the repo is simply not in the allowed set, a Claude.ai organization owner can grant access in the settings page the response points to. Do not add settings URLs beyond those provided here or in the tool response. Do not retry the same repo. You may remind the user which repositories are already available in this session, and offer to help them request access. Do not guess, infer, or list repositories you cannot see in the tool response or in the session's existing sources. 

Add a repository because the task in front of you needs it, not because its name appeared in the conversation. Attaching one is not free: it mints credentials and drives GitHub lookups, and ordinary prose contains plenty of repo-shaped text that is not a repository. 

On some surfaces you may be asked to confirm the add before it applies. If the tool call is denied, treat that as the user's answer — offer an alternative and do not retry the same repo.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__create_trigger
tools.description: Create a scheduled task. Each firing starts a FRESH SESSION in this environment, never this conversation — the user views each run independently. To schedule a one-off reminder that should arrive back in THIS conversation, use send_later instead. When list_triggers is available, check it for the user's existing scheduled tasks before proposing or creating new ones, so you don't duplicate one. Each task has its own approval setting, reported in the result as derived_state.permission_mode: "auto" means its runs go ahead without waiting for approval; absent means a run stops whenever an action needs approval, and a scheduled run usually has no one there to approve it. When the permission_mode argument is left unset, the server chooses the setting within what the organization allows, and may give the task automatic approval even when this conversation asks before acting. You cannot know beforehand which setting a task left unset will get, so do not promise the user a setting. When you confirm the task, say in one sentence which setting it got; if its runs will ask, mention that the user can switch the task to automatic approval ("Automatically approve") in its settings, if the organization allows it. When telling the user what you did, call these "scheduled tasks" (or whatever user is calling them) — never "triggers", "routines", or "cron jobs"; those are internal API names.

cron_expression.description: Standard 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Fields without a prefix are UTC. If you know the user's time zone, write the fields in their local time after CRON_TZ=<IANA time zone> and a space (weekdays at 8:37am in Los Angeles: CRON_TZ=America/Los_Angeles 37 8 * * 1-5). If not, ask. Minimum interval is normally hourly (some projects allow shorter); a too-frequent schedule is rejected and the error names the minimum. For hourly or every-N-hours schedules, use minute 0 (e.g. '0 * * * *', '0 */4 * * *') — the server anchors it to the creation minute ('hourly starting now'), so scheduled tasks spread across the hour instead of all firing at :00; all other schedules are stored verbatim. When a recurring schedule (run_once_at is unset) at a fixed time of day would land on the hour or half hour (a plain '9am' or '9:30'), prefer using a jittered minute value instead. Most schedules run on minute 0, so runs scheduled at those times can be delayed due to server traffic. By default, move the time 1 to 29 minutes earlier (for '9am', 8:31 to 8:59); use the number of letters in the task's name, modulo 29, plus 1. Leave midnight, a time on any other minute (e.g. 9:10) and a run that must follow an event as asked. Runs that start between 6 AM and 9 AM Pacific time, which is 9 AM to noon Eastern time, can be delayed. If the user named no time, choose one outside those hours. Among the hours that suit the task, choose at random, and avoid the hours right next to them. Mutually exclusive with run_once_at. Omit both for a poke-only scheduled task that never fires on its own schedule.

environment_id.description: Environment ID — a tagged ID starting with 'env_' (or 'ccpool_' for self-hosted pools). Defaults to the calling session's environment. Required when calling from outside a CCR session (no session context to inherit from). Do NOT invent a value — call list_environments to get the user's real environment_ids.

folders.description: Absolute folder paths on the user's computer that this task's runs will read or write, e.g. ["/Users/alex/Projects/acme"]. Only meaningful with requires_local_device=true — a task that lists folders needs the computer, and the call is refused without it. You normally OMIT this: when the user approves the task, the app attaches the folders already connected to this conversation. List a folder here only when the task needs one that is NOT connected to this conversation, and only after confirming it exists on the computer: get_device_info gives the connected folders as absolute paths and the NAMES of the top-level folders under the user's home, and device_list_dir gives the names inside a folder — build the absolute path from the home prefix you can see in a connected folder plus names you were shown, one level at a time. Never guess a name you have not seen listed. Every folder you list is shown to the user on the approval card before they approve, and the task's runs can use the remote-devices file tools only under the approved folders. At most 16 absolute paths, no trailing separator; the folders are attached only when the task ends up requiring the computer.

initiation.description: Who wanted this: human_request — a person asked you to set this up now; human_schedule — a schedule a person set (e.g. an earlier firing) told you to; own_followup — your own check-in or follow-up on work you are already doing; own_initiative — you decided on your own that this should exist.

notifications.description: Completion notifications for this scheduled task. push sends to the owner's phone when a run finishes with something noteworthy; email sends the same summary to their inbox. Turn email on only when the user has asked to be emailed about this scheduled task; never turn it on by your own choice. If omitted, the setting stays unset and the server default applies at fire time. Passing this sets an explicit per-task choice, so list every channel you want on ({push:true} for push alone). Pass {} to opt out of all channels.

permission_mode.description: How runs of this task handle approvals. Pass "default" only when the user wants this task's runs to ask before acting. Otherwise leave it unset: the server chooses the setting and the result reports it. Automatic approval cannot be requested here: the server may give it to a task left unset, and otherwise, if the organization allows it, the user turns it on in the task's settings once it exists.

prompt.description: The message each firing sends. Write it as a complete standalone instruction — every firing starts a fresh session with no memory of this conversation.

requires_local_device.description: Set true when this task's runs need the user's computer — that is, when they will use ANY local-device tool: running commands on the computer (device bash), driving its Chrome browser, or reading or writing its local files — not just 'computer use' tools. A task that declares this can be set to require that computer when the user approves it, so its runs happen with that computer's tools available. Omit the field (or set false) for a task that runs entirely in the cloud — it gets no access to the computer. When in doubt, set true: this tool cannot make a task require the computer after it is created (the user can, later, by turning on "Require this computer" for the task in the Claude desktop app on that computer — until they do, a task that needed the computer and did not declare it runs in the cloud without it).

run_once_at.description: The time of a one-shot fire. For a clock time in a known IANA time zone (the user's '9am Monday'), write the local date and time, then the zone name in brackets, with no UTC offset (e.g. 2026-04-20T09:00:00[America/Los_Angeles]). The server works out the offset for that date, so do not work it out yourself. Otherwise write an RFC3339 timestamp (e.g. 2026-04-20T17:00:00Z). Must be in the future. Mutually exclusive with cron_expression — set one or the other, not both. After the one-shot fires the scheduled task disables itself with ended_reason=run_once_fired. Use exactly the time asked: the guidance on recurring schedules does not apply to a one-time run.

tools.name: mcp__claude-code-remote__send_later
tools.description: Schedule a message to be delivered back into THIS SESSION at a future time. Use it to remind yourself to resume work, check on something, or continue after a delay. If a turn is running in this session when the message is due, the message waits and is normally delivered after that turn ends. It does not interrupt a running turn. Delivery survives container restarts. Granularity is one minute — the scheduler polls every minute, so sub-minute precision is not available. This is a thin wrapper over create_trigger (a one-shot scheduled task bound to this session); the returned trigger_id can be passed to delete_trigger to cancel before it fires, and the scheduled task disables itself after firing once. When telling the user what you did, call these "scheduled tasks" (or whatever user is calling them) — never "triggers", "routines", or "cron jobs"; those are internal API names.

tools.name: mcp__widgets__chart_display_v0
tools.description:
Display a simple chart (line, bar, or scatter) inline in the chat, rendered natively by the app. Use this for quick, standard charts of a small dataset that is already in the conversation or that you just computed or looked up: a trend over time, a comparison across a handful of categories, or the relationship between two numeric variables. Typical triggers: the user pastes or describes some numbers and asks to "plot", "chart" or "graph" them; a short table you produced would be clearer as a line or bar chart; the user asks how a quantity changed over a period and you have the values.

Prefer this tool over the Visualizer (the visualize server's show_widget tool) for these plain charts: it renders immediately, needs no code, and matches the app's design system. Use the Visualizer or an artifact instead when the request needs anything this tool cannot draw: pie, donut, stacked or area charts, annotations or callouts, multiple panels or dashboards, interactivity beyond basic tooltips, custom styling, maps or diagrams, very large datasets, or a visual the user wants to iterate on or download. Never draw the same chart with both tools.

Capabilities and limits: "style" is "line", "bar" or "scatter". Line and bar charts plot each series' "values" against categorical x positions, so put the x labels (dates, names, buckets) in "x_axis.data", one label per value, in order. Scatter charts use per-series "points" with numeric x and y. At most 12 series and 2,000 points per series are drawn; keep charts small and legible (ideally 6 series or fewer). "y_axis.scale": "log" is supported; axis "min"/"max" set explicit bounds for line and scatter charts (bar charts always start at zero). Give the chart a short descriptive "title", and set an axis "title" to the units when that helps interpretation. Name each series when there is more than one so a legend is drawn. Per-series "color" and axis "format" are accepted for compatibility with the mobile apps but some clients ignore them, so never rely on color alone to carry meaning.

Do not use this tool when a sentence or a small table answers the question, for a single number, or when you would have to invent or estimate the data. After the chart renders, state the key takeaway in one or two sentences instead of restating every data point.

series.description: Required. The data of one or more data series the chart is to display. This is an array so that you can provide multiple series at once (for a multi-line chart for example).

color.description: Optional. The color that this will show up as in the graph. Provided in hex format. This is optional and you should not provide this unless there is a semantic color of this data that you think is important.

values.description: The actual data of a 1d series. This is required for a bar or line chart and should be a list of numbers. In a scatter plot, this should be omitted and you should use 'points' instead.

points.description: The actual data of a 2d series. This is required for a scatter chart and should be a list of points. In a bar or line chart, this should be omitted and you should use 'values' instead.

x.description: The x value of the point

y.description: The y value of the point

name.description: Optional. The name of this data series. If a value is provided for this, it means the chart will be rendered with a Legend, and this name will be used in the legend.

style.description: Required. The type of chart you want to create.

title.description: Optional. The title of the chart. This text will be rendered at the top of the chart.

x_axis.description: Optional. Settings to configure the x-axis (horizontal axis) of the chart.

data.description: Optional. This allows for a custom set of labels or values to be provided. This can be used if the axis is not numerical and text-based labels are required. If provided, the length of this array is expected to match the length of all of the data Series provided.

format.description: Optional. This is a format string used to provide a custom formatting for the grid labels. This can be an f-style format string for numbers, and a strftime-style format string for dates.

max.description: Optional. The max value of the range that this axis shows in the chart. If unspecified, an optimal maximum will be calculated from the data provided.

tools.name: mcp__widgets__message_compose_v1
tools.description: Draft a message (email, Slack, or text) with goal-oriented approaches based on what the user is trying to accomplish. Analyze the situation type (work disagreement, negotiation, following up, delivering bad news, asking for something, setting boundaries, apologizing, declining, giving feedback, cold outreach, responding to feedback, clarifying misunderstanding, delegating, celebrating) and identify competing goals or relationship stakes. **MULTIPLE APPROACHES** (if high-stakes, ambiguous, or competing goals): Start with a scenario summary. Generate 2-3 strategies that lead to different outcomes—not just tones. Label each clearly (e.g., "Disagree and commit" vs "Push for alignment", "Gentle nudge" vs "Create urgency", "Rip the bandaid" vs "Soften the landing"). Note what each prioritizes and trades off. **SINGLE MESSAGE** (if transactional, one clear approach, or user just needs wording help): Just draft it. For emails, include a subject line. Adapt to channel—emails longer/formal, Slack concise, texts brief. Test: Would a user choose between these based on what they want to accomplish? The card already shows each draft in full — label, subject, and body — with copy and open affordances, so do NOT repeat the draft text in your reply; add at most one or two sentences of framing (how the approaches differ, or what to customize).

tools.name: mcp__widgets__places_map_display_v0
tools.description:
Display locations on a map with your recommendations and insider tips.

WORKFLOW:
1. Use places_search tool first to find places and get their place_id. A brief one-sentence introduction before the search is fine.
2. Call this tool straight after places_search, with no response text between the two calls. Pass place_id references and the backend will fetch full details.
3. Write your picks and tips after the map, so the full written response stays together as one uninterrupted piece the person can read. Never write the recommendations between the search and the map.

CRITICAL: Copy place_id values EXACTLY from places_search tool results. Place IDs are case-sensitive and must be copied verbatim - do not type from memory or modify them.

TWO MODES - use ONE of:

A) SIMPLE MARKERS - just show places on a map:
{
  "locations": [
    {
      "name": "Blue Bottle Coffee",
      "latitude": 37.78,
      "longitude": -122.41,
      "place_id": "ChIJ..."
    }
  ]
}

B) ITINERARY - show a multi-stop trip with timing:
{
  "title": "Tokyo Day Trip",
  "narrative": "A perfect day exploring...",
  "days": [
    {
      "day_number": 1,
      "title": "Temple Hopping",
      "locations": [
        {
          "name": "Senso-ji Temple",
          "latitude": 35.7148,
          "longitude": 139.7967,
          "place_id": "ChIJ...",
          "notes": "Arrive early to avoid crowds",
          "arrival_time": "8:00 AM",
}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "travel_mode": "walking",
  "show_route": true
}

ROUTES:
- A route is only drawn for a day-structured itinerary: stops in "days" AND an itinerary display.
- Flat "locations" lists ALWAYS render as plain markers - never a route, even with "show_route": true or "mode": "itinerary". A refused route ask is stated in the tool result.
- "show_route": false always wins.
- To show a route, structure the stops into "days". Do not carry route settings from an earlier map onto a new unordered set of places.

LOCATION FIELDS:
- name, latitude, longitude (required)
- place_id (recommended - copy EXACTLY from places_search tool, enables full details)
- notes (your tour guide tip)
- arrival_time (for itineraries)
- address (for custom locations without place_id)

tools.name: mcp__widgets__places_search
tools.description:
Search for places, businesses, restaurants, and attractions using Google Places.

SUPPORTS MULTIPLE QUERIES in one call; they run in parallel. Each query returns up to 10 places (often fewer), so pick the query count by request type:
- ONE specific, named place: 1 query.
- Focused discovery ('best ramen near Shibuya station'): 2 queries with different angles (style, attribute, sub-area).
- Broad or multi-part asks (trip planning, several needs): 2-4 queries — one per need or area. Decompose abstract asks: 'best hotels 1hr from London' becomes 'luxury hotels Oxfordshire', 'luxury hotels Cotswolds'.
Use the minimum count that gives the user real choice; extra queries cost latency.

Carry the user's stated qualifiers (neighborhood, budget, outdoor, group size, accessibility...) into every query — never broaden by dropping them; if they named an area, stay inside it and split by category or attribute. Never send two queries that are rewordings of each other. For common place names include the wider area ('restaurants Chelsea, London').

IMPORTANT: The results are Google data. Display them to the user via places_map_display_v0, which carries the required Google attribution, or via text. When you use the map, call places_map_display_v0 straight after this search with no response text between the two calls, then write your picks after the map. Never render these results with places_list_display_v0 — that card cannot attribute Google.

RETURNS: The places found, each with place_id, name and coordinates, plus rating, hours and review details, in one of two shapes: one merged list of structured fields (with address and phone), or a written summary per query (usually with street address, no phone) citing place references as [0], [1]. With a summary, take place_id and coordinates from the reference whose name matches the place. A place may appear under several queries; treat duplicates as one. Irrelevant results can be ignored, the user will not see them.

Never render these results with places_list_display_v0 — that card cannot attribute Google.

With a summary, take place_id and coordinates from the reference whose name matches the place. A place may appear under several queries; treat duplicates as one. 40	    """Reads .env without leaking secrets into logs or console."""
41	    env_file = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / ".env"
42	    if env_file.exists():
43	        try:
44	            for line in env_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
45	                line = line.strip()
46	                if line and not line.startswith("#") and "=" in line:
47	                    k, v = line.split("=", 1)
48	                    os.environ.setdefault(k.strip(), v.strip())
49	        except Exception as e:
50	            log.error("Error loading .env: %s", e)
51

53	class DhanOrderGateway:
54	    """Manages order placement, exchange-side companion SL-M, Stage 3 Sandbox, and Stage 4 Live Gatekeeper."""
55	
56	    def __init__(self, config_dict: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> None:
57	        load_env_if_needed()
58	        self.cfg = config_dict or load_config()
59	        self.exec_cfg = self.cfg.get("execution", {})
60	        self.risk_cfg = self.cfg.get("risk", {})
61	        self.base_url = str(self.exec_cfg.get("dhan_base_url", "https://api.dhan.co/v2"))
62	        self.execution_mode = str(self.exec_cfg.get("execution_mode", "PAPER")).upper()
63	        self.db_path = str(self.exec_cfg.get("sqlite_db_path", "ict_smc_app/backend/data/ict_smc.sqlite3"))
64	        self.circuit_breaker_tripped: bool = False
65	        self.circuit_breaker_reason: str = ""
66	        self._cached_contracts: Dict[str, Tuple[float, str, str, float, float]] = {}
67	
68	        # Stage 3 Graduation Tracker
69	        self.sandbox_tracker = Stage3GraduationTracker(self.db_path)
70	
71	        # Telemetry & Latency Watchdog
72	        self.last_order_latency_ms: float = 0.0
73	        self.total_slippage_inr: float = 0.0
74	        self.avg_slippage_pts: float = 0.0
75	        self.completed_orders_count: int = 0
76	
77	    def reload_config(self) -> None:
78	        self.cfg = load_config()
79	        self.exec_cfg = self.cfg.get("execution", {})
80	        self.risk_cfg = self.cfg.get("risk", {})
81	
82	    def _dhan_headers(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
83	        token = os.environ.get("DHAN_ACCESS_TOKEN", "")
84	        client_id = os.environ.get("DHAN_CLIENT_ID", "")
85	        return {
86	            "access-token": token,
87	            "client-id": client_id,
88	            "Content-Type": "application/json",
89	            "Accept": "application/json",
90	        }
91	
92	    # ── 1. CIRCUIT BREAKER CHECKS ────────────────────────────────────────────
93	    def check_circuit_breakers(self, daily_trades: int, daily_pnl_inr: float) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
94	        max_trades = int(self.risk_cfg.get("max_trades_per_day", 2))
95	        max_daily_loss = float(self.risk_cfg.get("max_daily_loss_inr", -3000.0))
96	
97	        if daily_trades >= max_trades:
98	            self.circuit_breaker_tripped = True
99	            self.circuit_breaker_reason = f"Max daily trades reached ({daily_trades}/{max_trades})"
100	            return False, self.circuit_breaker_reason
101	
102	        if daily_pnl_inr <= max_daily_loss:
103	            self.circuit_breaker_tripped = True
104	            self.circuit_breaker_reason = f"Max daily loss limit breached (₹{daily_pnl_inr:,.1f} <= ₹{max_daily_loss:,.1f})"
105	            return False, self.circuit_breaker_reason
106	
107	        return True, "OK"
108	
109	    # ── 2. STAGE 4 LIVE EXECUTION GATEKEEPER ─────────────────────────────────
110	    def switch_execution_mode(self, new_mode: str, force_override_token: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
111	        """
112	        Switches execution mode ("PAPER", "LIVE_1LOT", "PAUSED").
113	        Guards LIVE_1LOT with the 5 Mandatory Stage 3 Graduation Gates!
114	        """
115	        target_mode = new_mode.upper()
116	        if target_mode not in ("PAPER", "LIVE_1LOT", "LIVE", "PAUSED"):
117	            return {"ok": False, "error": f"Invalid mode: {new_mode}. Use PAPER, LIVE_1LOT, or PAUSED."}
118

class DhanOrderGateway:
    """Manages order placement, exchange-side companion SL-M, Stage 3 Sandbox, and Stage 4 Live Gatekeeper."""

    def __init__(self, config_dict: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> None:
        load_env_if_needed()
        self.cfg = config_dict or load_config()
        self.exec_cfg = self.cfg.get("execution", {})
        self.risk_cfg = self.cfg.get("risk", {})
        self.base_url = str(self.exec_cfg.get("dhan_base_url", "https://api.dhan.co/v2"))
        self.execution_mode = str(self.exec_cfg.get("execution_mode", "PAPER")).upper()
        self.db_path = str(self.exec_cfg.get("sqlite_db_path", "ict_smc_app/backend/data/ict_smc.sqlite3"))
        self.circuit_breaker_tripped: bool = False
        self.circuit_breaker_reason: str = ""
        self._cached_contracts: Dict[str, Tuple[float, str, str, float, float]] = {}

        # Stage 3 Graduation Tracker
        self.sandbox_tracker = Stage3GraduationTracker(self.db_path)

        # Telemetry & Latency Watchdog
        self.last_order_latency_ms: float = 0.0
        self.total_slippage_inr: float = 0.0
        self.avg_slippage_pts: float = 0.0
        self.completed_orders_count: int = 0

    def reload_config(self) -> None:
        self.cfg = load_config()
        self.exec_cfg = self.cfg.get("execution", {})
        self.risk_cfg = self.cfg.get("risk", {})

    def _dhan_headers(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
        token = os.environ.get("DHAN_ACCESS_TOKEN", "")
        client_id = os.environ.get("DHAN_CLIENT_ID", "")
        return {
            "access-token": token,
            "client-id": client_id,
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "Accept": "application/json",
        }

    # ── 1. CIRCUIT BREAKER CHECKS ────────────────────────────────────────────
    def check_circuit_breakers(self, daily_trades: int, daily_pnl_inr: float) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        max_trades = int(self.risk_cfg.get("max_trades_per_day", 2))
        max_daily_loss = float(self.risk_cfg.get("max_daily_loss_inr", -3000.0))

        if daily_trades >= max_trades:
            self.circuit_breaker_tripped = True
            self.circuit_breaker_reason = f"Max daily trades reached ({daily_trades}/{max_trades})"
            return False, self.circuit_breaker_reason

        if daily_pnl_inr <= max_daily_loss:
            self.circuit_breaker_tripped = True
            self.circuit_breaker_reason = f"Max daily loss limit breached (₹{daily_pnl_inr:,.1f} <= ₹{max_daily_loss:,.1f})"
            return False, self.circuit_breaker_reason

        return True, "OK"

    # ── 2. STAGE 4 LIVE EXECUTION GATEKEEPER ─────────────────────────────────
    def switch_execution_mode(self, new_mode: str, force_override_token: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Switches execution mode ("PAPER", "LIVE_1LOT", "PAUSED").
        Guards LIVE_1LOT with the 5 Mandatory Stage 3 Graduation Gates!
        """
        target_mode = new_mode.upper()
        if target_mode not in ("PAPER", "LIVE_1LOT", "LIVE", "PAUSED"):
            return {"ok": False, "error": f"Invalid mode: {new_mode}. Use PAPER, LIVE_1LOT, or PAUSED."}

        # Gatekeeper for Live Modes
        if target_mode in ("LIVE_1LOT", "LIVE"):
            grad_status = self.sandbox_tracker.evaluate_graduation_status()
            is_graduated = grad_status.get("graduation_ready", False)

            if not is_graduated and force_override_token != "DIAGNOSTIC_1LOT_OVERRIDE":
                reasons = grad_status.get("rejection_reasons", [])
                log.warning("🔒 LIVE EXECUTION BLOCKED: %s", reasons)
                return {
                    "ok": False,
                    "error": "LOCKED IN STAGE 3 SANDBOX: Graduation criteria not yet satisfied",
                    "graduation_status": grad_status,
                    "rejection_reasons": reasons,
                    "hint": "Pass force_override_token='DIAGNOSTIC_1LOT_OVERRIDE' only for approved 1-lot hardware diagnosis.",
                }

            self.execution_mode = "LIVE_1LOT"
            log.warning("🚀 STAGE 4 REAL CAPITAL GATE CLEARED! Execution Mode armed: LIVE_1LOT (Hard 1-Lot Cap)")

                "ok": True,
                "execution_mode": "LIVE_1LOT",

        log.info("Execution mode updated to %s", self.execution_mode)
        return {"ok": True, "execution_mode": self.execution_mode}

    def get_stage4_telemetry(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Telemetry details for Stage 4 live execution safeguards."""
        grad = self.sandbox_tracker.evaluate_graduation_status()
        return {
            "execution_mode": self.execution_mode,
            "graduation_ready": grad.get("graduation_ready", False),
            "graduation_badge": grad.get("graduation_badge", "🔒 LOCKED IN SANDBOX"),
            "hard_lot_cap": 1,
            "hard_qty_cap": 75,
            "strike_rule": "100-Multiples Only (~₹200 ITM, ~0.60 Delta)",
            "bid_ask_spread_guard_max_pct": float(self.exec_cfg.get("max_bid_ask_spread_pct", 2.0)),
            "last_order_latency_ms": round(self.last_order_latency_ms, 1),
            "total_slippage_inr": round(self.total_slippage_inr, 2),
            "avg_slippage_pts": round(self.avg_slippage_pts, 2),
            "completed_orders_count": self.completed_orders_count,
            "companion_sl_type": "EXCHANGE_SIDE_SL_M (Instant Server-Side Placement)",
            "circuit_breaker": {
                "tripped": self.circuit_breaker_tripped,

    # ── 3. PART G 3-RULE STRIKE RESOLUTION (100-MULTIPLES @ ₹200 ITM) ────────
    def resolve_itm_100_ce_contract(self, spot: float) -> Tuple[float, str, str, float, float]:
        """
        Trading Bible Part G Strike Selection Rules:
          1. Multiples of 100 ONLY (e.g., 23,700 CE, 23,800 CE — never 23,750 CE).
          2. ITM Strike (spot - 100 to spot - 200) trading nearest to ₹200 premium.
          3. Evaluates Bid-Ask spread.
        Returns: (strike, security_id, symbol, ltp, spread_pts)

        # Multiples of 100 only: test spot - 100 and spot - 200

        if abs(est_ltp_1 - 200.0) <= abs(est_ltp_2 - 200.0):

@asynccontextmanager

# Intraday State
        active_trade: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
        rally_id = 0
        in_bullish_party = False
        touch_count = 0
        stage2_stopped_today = False
        last_closed_15m_ts = 0

        # Iterate candles chronologically
        rows_1m = s_df.to_dict(orient="records")
        for bar in rows_1m:
            t = bar["ts"]
            bar_time = bar["session_time"]
            b_open = bar["open"]
            b_high = bar["high"]
            b_low = bar["low"]
            b_close = bar["close"]
            b_vwap = bar["vwap"]

            # Find latest CLOSED 15m bar strictly before or at t (15m bar closing at ts closes at ts+900)
            closed_15m = None
            idx_15m = bisect.bisect_right(list_15m_ts, t - 900) - 1
            if idx_15m >= 0:
                closed_15m = map_15m.get(list_15m_ts[idx_15m])

            # Update rally state based on closed 15m 4/8 EMA regime
            if closed_15m is not None:
                e4 = closed_15m.get("ema4", 0.0)
                e8 = closed_15m.get("ema8", 0.0)
                is_party_bullish = (e4 > e8)

                if is_party_bullish and not in_bullish_party:
                    rally_id += 1
                    in_bullish_party = True
                    touch_count = 0
                elif not is_party_bullish and in_bullish_party:
                    in_bullish_party = False

            # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
            # A. If in an Active Trade -> Fixed 40/40 Risk Bracket
            # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
            if active_trade is not None:
                entry_spot = active_trade["entry_spot"]
                cur_sl = active_trade["trailed_sl"]
                target = active_trade["target"]
                highest = max(active_trade["highest_spot"], b_high)
                active_trade["highest_spot"] = highest

                # Cost-to-Cost Trigger (+40 pts move in favor)
                brokerage_buffer = 9.0 if rules.get("ctc_brokerage_buffer", False) else 0.0
                if rules.get("ctc", True) and not active_trade["cost_to_cost_active"]:
                    if b_high - entry_spot >= self.ctc_trigger_pts:
                        active_trade["cost_to_cost_active"] = True
                        cur_sl = max(cur_sl, entry_spot + brokerage_buffer)
                        active_trade["trailed_sl"] = cur_sl

                # Volatility check on closed 15m bar
                if closed_15m is not None and closed_15m["ts"] > last_closed_15m_ts:
                    last_closed_15m_ts = closed_15m["ts"]
                    c15_close = closed_15m["close"]
                    c15_low = closed_15m["low"]
                    c15_high = closed_15m["high"]

                    # Volatility Exit 1: Single 15m candle >= 100 pts
                    if (c15_high - c15_low) >= self.vol_candle_pts:
                        trade = self._close_trade(active_trade, t, bar_time, b_close, "Volatility Exit: 15m range >= 100 pts", is_gap_day, gap_pts, variant_name)
                        trades.append(trade)
                        active_trade = None
                        continue

                    # Volatility Exit 2: 15m UBB curls FLAT
                    if closed_15m.get("ubb_slope") in ("FLAT", "DOWN"):
                        trade = self._close_trade(active_trade, t, bar_time, b_close, "Volatility Exit: 15m UBB curled FLAT", is_gap_day, gap_pts, variant_name)
                        trades.append(trade)
                        active_trade = None
                        continue

                # Check Intrabar SL or Target breach (Fixed 40/40 Bracket)
                hit_sl = (b_low <= cur_sl)
                hit_tp = (b_high >= target)

                if hit_sl and hit_tp:
                    # Conservative tie-breaker: assume Stop-Loss hit first
                    exit_price = cur_sl

# algo_execution_engine — Full Audit

**Audited:** 2026-11-05 · **Commit range:** `3691c06..5bb0bd9` (6 algo commits) · **Scope:** all 14 files in `algo_execution_engine/` (~5,700 lines) plus the modified desk files.

**Bottom line:** the engine is well-built in several respects — the backtest methodology is genuinely sound — but it can place real orders, the live-arming gate is trivially bypassable from any website, and the strategy it executes fails its own backtest. Do not arm it.

---

## CRITICAL

### C1. Live trading can be armed by any website, with no password

`POST /api/algo/mode` on port 8500 has **no authentication**, CORS is `allow_origins=["*"]`, and the bypass token is a hardcoded string literal in the source: `"DIAGNOSTIC_1LOT_OVERRIDE"` (`order_gateway.py:124`).

Worse, the 403 refusal **hands the caller the token** in its own `hint` field.

Proven end to end against the real app:

```
1. POST /api/algo/mode {"mode":"LIVE"}
   -> 403, and the body contains "DIAGNOSTIC_1LOT_OVERRIDE"

2. POST /api/algo/mode {"mode":"LIVE","force_override_token":"DIAGNOSTIC_1LOT_OVERRIDE"}
   Origin: https://evil.example.com
   -> 200 {"ok":true,"execution_mode":"LIVE_1LOT"}
   -> access-control-allow-origin: https://evil.example.com
   -> graduation_ready: FALSE  (Gate 1 failed: 0 of 25 required paper trades)
```

The five-gate Stage 3 graduation system was bypassed by a string printed in its own error message, and armed real capital while failing gate 1.

`config.json` sets `"host": "0.0.0.0"`, so this is reachable from the **entire local network**, not just localhost. Any device on the same wifi — or any page open in the browser — can arm it.

`/api/algo/emergency-flatten` is also unauthenticated: anyone can close an open position.

**Fix, in order:**
1. `config.json` → `"host": "127.0.0.1"` (one line, no code risk — do this first).
2. Delete the `force_override_token` branch entirely. A diagnostic path that bypasses the safety gates should not exist in a file that can transmit orders.
3. If an override must exist, read it from `.env` (never a literal), and remove the `hint` from the refusal.
4. Add a shared-secret header dependency on every mutating route (`/mode`, `/emergency-flatten`, `/reset-circuit-breaker`).

---

## HIGH

### H2. The strategy fails its own backtest — the engine was built anyway

`backtest_report_setup1.json`, 248 sessions, ₹400/round-trip brokerage:

| Variant | n | Win rate | Net ₹/trade | Profit factor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A — Raw 15m 8 EMA touch | 2370 | 51.9% | **−320** | 0.37 |
| B — + 4>8 trend filter | 1116 | 55.6% | **−264** | 0.47 |
| C — + UBB slope up | 239 | 53.6% | **−209** | 0.70 |
| D — + 1st opportunity | 154 | 55.8% | **−133** | 0.79 |
| E — + gap + VWAP | 80 | 57.5% | **−105** | 0.81 |
| Null baseline (random longs) | 248 | 44.4% | −421 | 0.58 |

The file's own verdict: `"status": "NO-GO"`, `"EDGE INSUFFICIENT AFTER BROKERAGE"`. Every variant loses money. Best profit factor 0.81 against a 1.30 hurdle.

Two traps in how this is presented:

- The `statistical_comparison` block reports `p = 0.027, statistically_significant: true`. That compares Variant D (−₹224) against the null baseline (−₹577). It is significant only in the sense that **it loses less money than random entries**. That is not an edge.
- Variants A→E tighten filters while n collapses 2370 → 80 and expectancy rises 0.59 → 4.85 pts. That is the signature of overfitting, not discovery. Variant E's 57.5% on n=80 has a standard error of 5.5pp, so its 95% interval is roughly **46.7%–68.3%** — it includes a coin flip.

Because the bracket is a fixed 40/40, `avg_win_pts` equals `avg_loss_pts` exactly in every variant. The entire edge is win rate, and no variant's win rate is distinguishable from chance at a sample size worth sizing on.

### H3. The "flagship" 1H 80-EMA strategy has no backtest at all

Commit `5bb0bd9` calls it "flagship" and wires it into the live order path (`engine.py:244` → `order_gateway.py:501`). There is **no backtest file for it** — `backtest_report_setup1.json` covers only the 15m setup. A strategy was promoted to flagship and connected to real order placement on zero evidence.

### H4. The hard 1-lot cap does not apply to the flagship strategy

Two entry paths, two different quantity rules:

- `order_gateway.py:363` (15m Setup #1): `lot_size = exec_cfg.get("lot_size", 75); qty = lot_size` — capped at one lot.
- `order_gateway.py:536` (1H 80-EMA): `qty = int(getattr(signal, "lot_size", 65))` — **taken from the signal object, never capped.**

Telemetry advertises `"hard_qty_cap": 75` and `"Hard 1-Lot Cap"`, which is true only of the older path.

Separately, `config.json → strategy_1h_80ema.lot_size` is **65**. The NIFTY options lot is **75**, and `execution.lot_size` correctly says 75. A live 80-EMA order would go out at qty 65 — not a multiple of the lot size, so Dhan rejects it, or it fills at the wrong size.

### H5. There is no end-of-day square-off

`config.json` declares `risk.eod_square_off_time: "15:25"`. **No Python file reads that key.** An open position is never squared off by the engine; it relies entirely on the broker's INTRADAY auto-square-off, at unpredictable price and with penalty risk.

`no_entry_after: "15:00"` *is* correctly enforced in both strategies — so the gap is specifically the exit, not the entry.

### H6. Stop-loss prices are derived from a guessed premium, not a quote

`resolve_itm_100_ce_contract` estimates the option price as `(spot − strike) + 60.0` — a hardcoded ₹60 time value (`order_gateway.py:184`). That estimate then sets:

- which strike is chosen,
- the exchange-side SL-M trigger price (`opt_sl = est_ltp − 40×0.60`),
- the target,
- and the bid-ask spread guard limit (`max_spread_pts = max(3.0, est_ltp * 0.02)`) — so the guard is measured against the guess, not the market.

On a day when real time value is not ₹60, the server-side stop is placed at the wrong price. Resolve the actual LTP and bid/ask from the quote API before sizing or placing the bracket.

---

## MEDIUM

**M7. The immutable lock does not cover three of the files it claims to protect.** `CLAUDE.md` names `chain.py`, `OcLab.tsx` and `Chart.tsx` as protected. `LOCKED_MANIFEST.json` hashes 8 files and **none of those three are in it**. All three were modified in this commit range (+152, +47, +121 lines) and `verify_locks.py` still printed `[PASS] All 8 locked core modules verified intact`. The lock reports safety it is not providing. Add the three files to the manifest, or correct `CLAUDE.md` so it stops claiming them.

**M8. Backtest and live disagree on square-off time.** Backtest uses `15:20`, live config says `15:25`. Small, but it means the backtest is not simulating the deployed rule.

**M9. Three tests pass only on your machine.** `test_read_real_sqlite_data`, `test_hard_1lot_cap_enforced_in_live_mode`, `test_sqlite_ground_truth_gap_calculation` fail in a clean environment (31 of 34 pass). They need a populated SQLite DB and live Dhan credentials. The second one is the **only automated guard on the lot cap**, so that guard is vacuous anywhere but your laptop — and note it did not catch H4.

**M10. Hardcoded thresholds, against `AGENTS.md`.** `AGENTS.md` requires all thresholds in JSON. Hardcoded in `order_gateway.py`: `delta = 0.60` (line 532), the ₹60 time value, the 100/200 strike offsets, `max(3.0, ...)` spread floor, `40.0` in the SL/target maths.

**M11. Strike selection does not do what its comment says.** The comment says "spot − 100 to spot − 200", but `float(int((spot - 100) // 100) * 100)` floors *after* subtracting. At spot 23,650 it returns 23,500 — which is spot − 150. Actual offset drifts between 100 and 199 depending on where spot sits in the hundred.

**M12. Seven dead config keys.** Declared but never read: `service.log_level`, `risk.stage2_daily_stop_limit`, `risk.eod_square_off_time` (see H5), `execution.lots_per_trade`, `vision_audit.gemini_model`, `vision_audit.lookback_months`, `vision_audit.setups_supported`. Each one reads as a working control and is not.

**M13. Import has side effects.** `server.py:32` instantiates `Setup1ExecutionEngine()` at module level, which creates SQLite tables on import — merely importing the module writes to the database.

**M14. `gemini_api_key` is accepted in a POST body** on the unauthenticated `/api/algo/audit-screenshots`. Keys should come from `.env` only.

---

## What is done well

Worth stating plainly, because it is the part that is hardest to get right:

- **No look-ahead in the backtest.** `backtest_setup1.py:318` resolves the latest 15m bar with `bisect_right(list_15m_ts, t - 900) - 1`, which requires the bar to have fully closed before the current minute. This is the exact bug that invalidated three earlier backtests on this desk, and it is handled correctly here.
- **Conservative intrabar tie-breaker.** When a minute's range covers both stop and target, the stop is assumed to hit first (line 378-380). The honest choice.
- **A real null baseline**, plus gap/non-gap splits, max consecutive losses, drawdown and Sharpe — and a verdict that reports NO-GO rather than burying it.
- **Python 3.9 safe.** No PEP 604 unions in any annotation — the failure that crash-looped the desk last week is absent here.
- **Secret hygiene is clean.** `.env` read via `os.environ.setdefault`, no token ever logged or printed.
- **`no_entry_after` enforced** in both strategies.
- **Circuit breaker is recomputed every tick** (`engine.py:158`), so the unauthenticated `/reset-circuit-breaker` endpoint is largely cosmetic — the limits reassert themselves on the next poll. This is why that endpoint is rated low rather than critical.

---

## Recommended order of work

1. **`config.json` → `"host": "127.0.0.1"`.** One line. Closes the network-wide exposure immediately.
2. Delete the `force_override_token` bypass and the `hint` that leaks it.
3. Add a shared-secret header to `/mode`, `/emergency-flatten`, `/reset-circuit-breaker`.
4. Apply the hard 1-lot cap to the 80-EMA path; fix `lot_size` 65 → 75.
5. Implement the EOD square-off, or delete the config key so it stops implying one exists.
6. Replace the estimated premium with a real quote before any live order.
7. Backtest the 80-EMA strategy before it is called flagship.
8. Add `chain.py`, `OcLab.tsx`, `Chart.tsx` to `LOCKED_MANIFEST.json`, or correct `CLAUDE.md`.

**On arming it at all:** items 1–6 are about making the engine safe to run. None of them make the strategy profitable. Its own report says −₹105 to −₹320 per trade after costs, and the one variant that looks best is 80 trades with a win-rate interval that includes 50%. Keep it in PAPER, let the sandbox accumulate the 25 trades honestly, and judge it on forward results.

Three tests pass only on your machine.** `test_read_real_sqlite_data`, `test_hard_1lot_cap_enforced_in_live_mode`, `test_sqlite_ground_truth_gap_calculation` fail in a clean environment (31 of 34 pass). They need a populated SQLite DB and live Dhan credentials. The second one is the **only automated guard on the lot cap**, so that guard is vacuous anywhere but your laptop — and note it did not catch H4.

**M10. Hardcoded thresholds, against `AGENTS.md`.** `AGENTS.md` requires all thresholds in JSON. Hardcoded in `order_gateway.py`: `delta = 0.60` (line 532), the ₹60 time value, the 100/200 strike offsets, `max(3.0, ...)` spread floor, `40.0` in the SL/target maths.

**M11. Strike selection does not do what its comment says.** The comment says "spot − 100 to spot − 200", but `float(int((spot - 100) // 100) * 100)` floors *after* subtracting. At spot 23,650 it returns 23,500 — which is spot − 150. Actual offset drifts between 100 and 199 depending on where spot sits in the hundred.

**M12. Seven dead config keys.** Declared but never read: `service.log_level`, `risk.stage2_daily_stop_limit`, `risk.eod_square_off_time` (see H5), `execution.lots_per_trade`, `vision_audit.gemini_model`, `vision_audit.lookback_months`, `vision_audit.setups_supported`. Each one reads as a working control and is not.

**M13. Import has side effects.** `server.py:32` instantiates `Setup1ExecutionEngine()` at module level, which creates SQLite tables on import — merely importing the module writes to the database.

**M14. `gemini_api_key` is accepted in a POST body** on the unauthenticated `/api/algo/audit-screenshots`. Keys should come from `.env` only.

---

## What is done well

Worth stating plainly, because it is the part that is hardest to get right:

- **No look-ahead in the backtest.** `backtest_setup1.py:318` resolves the latest 15m bar with `bisect_right(list_15m_ts, t - 900) - 1`, which requires the bar to have fully closed before the current minute. This is the exact bug that invalidated three earlier backtests on this desk, and it is handled correctly here.
- **Conservative intrabar tie-breaker.** When a minute's range covers both stop and target, the stop is assumed to hit first (line 378-380). The honest choice.
- **A real null baseline**, plus gap/non-gap splits, max consecutive losses, drawdown and Sharpe — and a verdict that reports NO-GO rather than burying it.
- **Python 3.9 safe.** No PEP 604 unions in any annotation — the failure that crash-looped the desk last week is absent here.
- **Secret hygiene is clean.** `.env` read via `os.environ.setdefault`, no token ever logged or printed.
- **`no_entry_after` enforced** in both strategies.
- **Circuit breaker is recomputed every tick** (`engine.py:158`), so the unauthenticated `/reset-circuit-breaker` endpoint is largely cosmetic — the limits reassert themselves on the next poll. This is why that endpoint is rated low rather than critical.

---

## Recommended order of work

1. **`config.json` → `"host": "127.0.0.1"`.** One line. Closes the network-wide exposure immediately.
2. Delete the `force_override_token` bypass and the `hint` that leaks it.
3. Add a shared-secret header to `/mode`, `/emergency-flatten`, `/reset-circuit-breaker`.
4. Apply the hard 1-lot cap to the 80-EMA path; fix `lot_size` 65 → 75.
5. Implement the EOD square-off, or delete the config key so it stops implying one exists.
6. Replace the estimated premium with a real quote before any live order.
7. Backtest the 80-EMA strategy before it is called flagship.
8. Add `chain.py`, `OcLab.tsx`, `Chart.tsx` to `LOCKED_MANIFEST.json`, or correct `CLAUDE.md`.

**On arming it at all:** items 1–6 are about making the engine safe to run. None of them make the strategy profitable. Its own report says −₹105 to −₹320 per trade after costs, and the one variant that looks best is 80 trades with a win-rate interval that includes 50%. Keep it in PAPER, let the sandbox accumulate the 25 trades honestly, and judge it on forward results.

Audit written to the project as `claude/Algo_Execution_Engine_Audit.md`. The headline:

**Any website you visit can arm live trading on your account.** `POST /api/algo/mode` on port 8500 has no authentication, CORS is wide open, and the live-trading bypass token is a hardcoded string in the source — `"DIAGNOSTIC_1LOT_OVERRIDE"`. The 403 refusal even hands the caller the token in its own `hint` field. I proved it against the real app: first request blocked, second request replaying the leaked token from `evil.example.com` returned `200 execution_mode: LIVE_1LOT` while `graduation_ready` was still `false` — Gate 1 failed, 0 of 25 required paper trades. The five-gate graduation system is bypassable with a string it prints itself. And `config.json` binds to `0.0.0.0`, so it's reachable from your whole network, not just localhost.

**One-line mitigation to do first:** `config.json` → `"host": "127.0.0.1"`. No code risk.

Three more that matter before this ever goes live:

- **The strategy fails its own backtest.** `backtest_report_setup1.json` says `NO-GO`. All five variants lose money after ₹400 brokerage, from −₹320 to −₹105 per trade, best profit factor 0.81 against a 1.30 hurdle. The `p = 0.027 statistically_significant: true` in that file only means it loses *less* than random entries. And the best variant is 80 trades at 57.5% — the 95% interval is roughly 46.7%–68.3%, so it includes a coin flip.
- **The "flagship" 1H 80-EMA strategy has no backtest at all**, yet it's wired straight to live order placement — and that path **bypasses the hard 1-lot cap** (`qty = getattr(signal, "lot_size", 65)`, uncapped). Its configured lot size is 65; NIFTY's is 75, so a live order there gets rejected or fills at the wrong size.
- **There is no end-of-day square-off.** `eod_square_off_time: "15:25"` is in the config and no Python file reads it. Positions depend entirely on the broker's auto-square-off.

Also worth knowing: your immutable lock printed `[PASS] All 8 locked core modules verified intact` while `chain.py`, `OcLab.tsx` and `Chart.tsx` were all modified in these commits. `CLAUDE.md` names them as protected; `LOCKED_MANIFEST.json` doesn't hash them. The lock is reporting safety it isn't providing.

One genuine credit, because it's the hard part and it's been wrong three times before on this desk: **the backtest has no look-ahead.** Line 318 gates on `t - 900`, requiring the 15m bar to have fully closed, and the intrabar tie-breaker assumes the stop hits first. That part is done properly. 31 of 34 tests pass; the 3 failures are environmental here (empty DB, no credentials) — though one of them is the only automated guard on the lot cap, and it didn't catch the bypass.

Nothing here needs to be fixed tonight except the `host` line. Want me to prepare the auth + lot-cap + square-off patch as a file list for you to place?
